item.title: Crafting Shape in a Fluid World – The Intersection of Marketing and External Forces
item.content:encoded:
Marketing practice is being transformed by technological advances, geopolitical shifts, economic pressures, and growing demands for sustainability and social responsibility. Retail environments serve as key sites where these transformations unfold, with both physical and digital channels becoming laboratories for new consumer engagement and adaptive strategies. Consumers now demand greater brand ethics, transparency, and societal contributions, while external disruptions like supply chain fragility, inflation, and geopolitical tensions reshape pricing and sourcing. Simultaneously, artificial intelligence and platform ecosystems are fundamentally changing how consumers access information and make purchase decisions.

Appel publié par Journal of Consumer Marketing. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Consumer responses to global disruptions (e.g., inflation, supply chain fragility, climate events, tariffs, war)
  • Impact of AI, automation, and platform-based ecosystems on consumer well-being and happiness
  • How to enhance responsible consumption (e.g., reducing food waste and increasing adoptions of green energy and public transportation)
  • How to serve marginalized and disadvantaged consumers and enhance equality among gender, race, ethnicity, and socioeconomic status through marketing and equitable practices
  • Evolving consumer purchase patterns and consumption practices around brand ethics, transparency, and sustainability
  • How firms can navigate sociopolitical activism (e.g., Should brands take a stand or remain silent?)
  • Recalibrating brand-consumer relationships in times of social and political polarization
  • Cross-cultural and cross-generational consumer insights in a post-globalization era
  • Retail innovation in response to external forces, trends, disruptions, and shifting consumer expectations
  • Marketing strategies for enhancing trust, loyalty, engagement in uncertain environments

Timeline

  • August 15, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • October 15, 2026: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Transforming Retail and Consumer Marketing Strategies in the Era of the Digital Economy
item.content:encoded:
Aboobucker Ilmudeen, South Eastern University of Sri Lanka

Alaa A. Qaffas, University of Jeddah

The digital economy has fundamentally restructured retail and consumer marketing, blurring boundaries between physical and virtual commerce while intensifying competitive pressures. Consumer expectations now center on personalization, authenticity, and social responsibility, with social media and mobile platforms playing critical roles in shaping purchasing decisions. This transformation presents both opportunities for businesses to strengthen customer relationships through digital tools and challenges related to technology access, market fragmentation, and legacy system integration.

This special issue invites research examining how businesses are adapting retail and marketing strategies to succeed in digital-transformed markets. The editors seek contributions that explore the theoretical foundations, empirical evidence, and practical insights regarding digital transformation in retailing, consumer engagement, distribution systems, and business strategy to guide practitioners, policymakers, and scholars navigating contemporary market shifts.

Appel publié par The International Review of Retail, Distribution and Consumer Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Digital transformation in retail and consumer marketing
  • Omni-channel retail strategies and the integration of physical and virtual spaces
  • Evolution of consumer behavior in digital environments
  • Social media's role in brand trust and consumer identity
  • Mobile commerce and online marketplaces
  • Personalization and customer relationship management in digital contexts
  • Distribution channel innovation and supply chain management
  • Sustainability and corporate social responsibility in digital retail
  • Competitive strategies for businesses navigating digital disruption
  • Technology adoption barriers and digital divide in retail

Timeline

  • September 10, 2026: Manuscript deadline
